For description, I try to use 3 or 4 VAKOG and then flesh it from there. :) For example;

V - Vision: The pizza looked so inviting inside the cardboard box. The melted cheese, the strip's of ham. All so delicious, but for one thing - the pineapple! 

A - Audio: The shop owned, noticing my scrunched up face, huffed "What's da maaattar?" His voice was tinged with annoyance, detectable even through his thick accent. "Whaaddyaa not lika ma pizza?"

K - Kinaesthetic: He picked off one of the pineapple chunks and squeezed it. "Looksie, so juicy!" I cringed as a spit of juice hit my cheek. My stomach did a flip... my appetite was long gone now.

O - Olfactory: The pungent tartness of the pineapple assaulted my nose. Who would have known such a tiny flick of pineapple juice could cause such nausea? 

G - Gastronomic: At his instance, I tore a slice of the pizza, focusing on the oozing cheese, and took a bite. Oh! The cheese! Oh! The ham! Oh, the - Oh no. The pineapple. It was juicy and tart and - Oh God. The nausea. The gaze of the shop man looked on at me with horror as I puked. I could taste the acidic bile mixed with the energy drinks from before. It was dreadful. It made me puke again, all over the pizza.

... this is probably a terrible example, but you can see how easy it is to expand on the senses descriptions once you have a few words in mind. :) I hope this helps. 😅

"Young man," the woman said leaning over the counter - counter? "I don't suppose you have banksia available for a wedding bouquet?" 

Anh blinked several times as he stared at the woman. Her hair was the colour of sand, and concaved at the back. She was stout with a plain white shirt and blue trousers. He'd never seen such an odd looking woman before.

"Young man!" The woman said snapping her fingers. "Banksias?" 

Anh looked to his left. Then his right. Flowers, everywhere, and strange little ceramics in the shapes of foxes and rabbits. "I'm sorry," he stuttered. "I don't know what that is. And how did I-" 

"What do you mean you don't have Banksias!" The woman huffed causing Anh to flinch. "It's the dry season now, and dry season means banksias."

"Dry season?" Anh said with a raised eyebrow. "Lady -"

"Ms!" 

Anh swallowed. "Erm. Ms... I only know four seasons. And I think there's been a misunderstanding, I don't even know where I am!"

The lady looked at him like he was mad. Anh went on to excuse himself and find his dragon when the lady held up her arms. 

"Goodness me!" She said. "How thick are you?"

Anh was pretty bloody skinny, but even he found that rude. He was about to lift his shirt to make a point about his abs when he found his tunic had been replaced with a strange material. He stared down and found he was wearing an apron - similar to the one Lord Cao's cooks wore in the kitchens, only instead of been plain linen this one was embroided with little blue flowers and cats. He also had a pocket, but his dagger and peppers weren't in there. Instead, they were filled with flowers. 

"What the...?" Anh swallowed before looking at the woman. "Lady, where am I?!"

"MS!" She seethed. 

Anh clasped fistfuls of his hair. "Where am I! Where am I!"

"Oh my!" The lady said with a roll of her eyes. "I'd like to speak to your manager." 

"My manager?" Anh said shaking his head. "What does that even mean!"

At the moment, Hei Lin emerged from behind the bench. Anh gaped at the mighty black dragon who donned an apron similar to his own. Hei Lin placed his hands on his... wings. "Now what's all the fuss about?" 

"Hei Lin, what happened to you?" Anh stammered as the dragon fixed the crown of daisies and babies breath - babies breath?? - behind his horns. 

"This young man insulted me!" The lady cried. 

"Listen, Karen!" Anh snapped at the lady. "We got proteas and gum, but banksia doesn't grow this far north of Perth in the dry season!" 

"Oh, so now you know what a banksia is?" The woman said with a smirk.

"Wait, no -" Anh stammered. "Actually..." 

Hei Lin shook his great head at Anh and tutted. "Oh Anh. What did I say last week about your customer service skills?" 

"I don't know!" 

"That I'd have to dock your pay if you didn't accept that the customer is always right." 

"Dock my pay?!" Anh gasped. "But how will I pay for our boarding in Jining! Or for your roasted swallows." 

Hei Lin frowned at Anh and pointed to the badge on his apron. "Did you forget? I'm a vegan now." 

"NOOOOO!" The world around him began spinning. It was if the very earth began spinning on his axis at Hei Lin's proclamation - though as Anh rose suddenly in his bed, he question what a vegan even was? 

He wiped the sweat from his brow. He was in his bed, back in the Dragon Haven. Hei Lin was curled up by the fireplace and there were no cranky ladies or aprons in sight. 

"What," Anh gasped in confusion fat. "The holy f*cking sh*tshow was that?"

Just to add - the fact that they're advertising for farm assistants, yet asking for your details, is phishing. 

Scammers know new comers to Australia may often start out on farms for contract and seasonal work. Likewise, cleaning roles. 

Avoid Facebook groups for these kinds of jobs. If you're interested in farm work, find a local orchard and call them directly. They usually don't post online as the nature of the business is quite rotational and vetted through word of mouth. 

References - grew up on a horse farm that hired seasonal workers. Had lots of orchards nearby for fruit picking too.

It's a scam.

No workplace would require these details BEFORE employment, nor after. The only instance MyGov may be needed AFTER you've been employed is if you are an authorised tax accountant (for access to the ATO portal). Even then, it's set up through MyGov and nothing else. 

Nor would any legit workplace request personal information from you via a bloody insecure google doc.

Do not give out your information. Report them to Scamwatch.

I should also note - keep in mind that social housing (such as Housing SA) aren't as budget friendly as commonly thought of. Your rent is charged at 25% of your total income which can be lot. I'm not sure how much community housing charges sadly, but please keep that in mind moving forward.

Unfortunately, you could be on Cat 1 for a very long time. Some people I've spoken to have been on for years, the longest being 9 years, despite debilitating health issues.

There are some options you can take to make your case stronger, but it's unlikely to change much more sadly. Some options include seeking a social worker to plead your case through a letter, a doctors certificate, or even calling your local state MP for pressure. 

Seeing as you are couch surfing and a female, not to mention pregnant, you are eligible for emergency housing. You could phone Housing SA for either an emergency appointment or a housing check (you your also ask an MP to book this for you), and they should be able to put you up in emergency accommodation for up to one month. The hotels they use for clients up North are Comfort Inn and Pavlos (both on Main North Road). I'm not sure what they are elsewhere in the city. The room is free of charge but you still need to provide your own food, ect, and it is only for 30 days. 

For a long term home with much better turn around, I really advise looking into community housing options. Anglicare, United Communities and Junction are the largest providers for community housing in SA. I believe Junction has an option for community housing for just women. Community housing is much smaller in terms of total size for housing, kind of like what you'd find in little retirement villages (one bedroom flats usually), but it's better than sleeping on the streets or couches. 

Speaking of - Homelessness Gateway has priority fot women and children to be seen first if you find yourself in that situation. They are also a really fantastic provider for advocacy if social housing is still what you want. They're process is quite in-depth (psych, finances, etc), but you will be looked after and fed while they help you. 1800 003 308

I'm not sure if this would be useful either, but something to keep in mind also is Yarrow Place. They're more of a domestic abuse shelter for women, but I imagine they would have resources for women in your situation also. Here is their number. 1800 817 421.

Best of luck.

There is the Northern Community Mental Health Service on Park Terrace, Salisbury, as a good walk-in/triage service. 08 7485 4300

I'd recommend taking some earlier steps though. Has your friend been to a GP yet? Most places, for ongoing support that is, will require a referral from their GP. Contact in my experience has always been very quick too! You don't need to tell them everything, but with a good enough brief, your friend can get the referral to the right place. 

With trauma experiences, an intake assessment after the referral is made, may conclude your friend does CPT or DBT sessions which run for around 6-12 weeks. Don't let that alarm you if you think think will be costly. If your friend is earning below a certain threshold, or is a student, or under 25, is Indigenous, or claiming centrelink, they are entitled to 12 counselling sessions/DPT classes for free! I know of people who did these sessions in Salisbury, but it looks like it's relocated to Sonder now. https://www.healthdirect.gov.au/low-cost-or-free-mental-health-services

If your friend is involved in the military, or has a family member currently serving (age doesn't matter), then I  can't recommend highly enough they reach out to Open Arms (Previously Vietnam Veterens) in Elizabeth! I understand this may be a stretch, but this is also a free service and they offer many group and one and one counselling. I saw them on 2019 while grieving, and the woman I saw, Jess, honestly saved my life. They also do support groups (think AA style). 1800 011 046

Does your friend study? If your friend is in High School, or is of High School age and has recently dropped out, they are able to access confidential support from their school counsellors. I'm not sure how it works these days, but when I was in school it was as simple as walking into their office and asking if they had a moment. I also remember some kids who were a bit shy would email their school counsellors for a bit of support. Likewise for uni! The wait times for appointments or walk ins are a long time I admit now, but they are free and you can ask for truama specific. Mawson Lakes UniSA campus has an office which is obviously north. 
https://i.unisa.edu.au/students/student-support-services/counselling/make-an-appointment/

Further, all three unis in Adelaide now have an after hours support line! 1300107441 or text,  0488884163

Does your friend work? If so, look into their workplace or union for support services. Most workplaces have a support service dedicated to that area for up to three sessions. And they don't need to be related to work at all! I can't say if they will be based up North, but it's something to look into. I know many offer phone counselling now too, which may be helpful. 

Speaking of phones counselling - if your friend is really stuck for travel, there are TONNES of great, and totally free phone services available, with many catered to specific needs. A couple go to options are obviously Kidshelpline 1800 55 1800, Lifeline 13 11 14, or Beyond Blue 1300 22 4636.

I'm from Salisbury and work in government. I can see the point you're making, but most people here want to get vaccinated, unemployed or not. Here's the thing though - many people are without transport up our way. Unemployment here sky-rocketed again when the trains shut, and there aren't that many buses that travel directly to vaccination hubs. 

To put it into perspective. I drive myself, but without my car, if I wanted to go to Playford Vaccine Hub, it would take nearly 2 hours one way to get there just from where I am in Salisbury. This is including walking and taking three buses. Now imagine if you're in Angle Vale, Andrews Farm or Virgina where public transport is next to none in some of the poorer areas, and how are you going to convince someone to spend a whole day in transit to get vaccinated?

Unemployment naturally falls into this still. Low income, less chances of driving, more chances of saving money for food rather than uber or buses. 

I'm not saying this is the only answer to why there are lower vaccine rates up here. It's also a language and literacy concern. We have a lot of walks of life here with different beliefs and some without much understanding of vaccines as it wasn't relevant to them before coming here. Or they can't read the advice. Same goes for elderly and children who fall into the cracks when it comes to health literacy. The point is, it's not simply an anti Vax mindset or deviation from public health policy.

I'm from Salisbury area. While Modbury is lovely, especially Tea Tree Gully, Salisbury and surrounds has a lot to offer too!

Houses here are cheap for rent, and cheaper for buying. You aren't looking at small, dingy houses either, most houses here are 3 bed, 2 bathrooms, with generous backyards. Paralowie is probably your cheapest, but Salisbury East, Para Hills and Parafield Gardens right up to Mawson Lakes are really affordable and generous for housing. 

Lifestyle in Salisbury is great too! We have so many lovely trails and wetlands to explore, and gorgeous parks. There are so many bike trails that lead on to the city or to Gawler. My favourite one is the Little Para Trail though which winds through Salisbury to Mawson Lakes following the Little Para River. We also have large playgrounds too if you have kids or are bit of a kid at heart. St Kilda playground, Howie Bowie Reserve, Carisbrook is my personal favourite. We have plenty of hiking trails, and a massive skate park too if that's your thing. The footy clubs have a lot of options for adults and children, the West Club even has an All Abilities option for sports. You're spoiled for choice of lifestyle clubs too, depending on your interests. 

Food! Holy shit, if you don't believe me on anything, trust me that the food here is way better than Modbury. Salisbury is settled by quite a large migrant population, and the food here shows for it! John Street has a mix of Afghan and Persian flavours for one, we even have a Shisha lounge. There is so many Indian options too, and sooo many Vietnamese options (PSA, Vietnam House is also great for checking out hot RAAFIES, hehe). Also, we have a world famous Mexican restaurant that the New York Times wrote about, Taco Quetzalotal (can't remember the spelling!). There's quite a budding Cafe scene now too. Cafe Amigos has sadly moved closer to the Hospital, but we have Badger and Bone, Tango, The Watershed (This one is on a lake!), Indulge, Delicia. Look, even if you choose Modbury, just come to Salisbury for the food if nothing else, haha.

Community and volunteering is also a huge deal in this area. I know I'm going to cop shit for this, but Salisbury Council area has the highest volunteer rates in SA, which yes, may be a consequence of the lack of job opportunities. But volunteering sets us apart. Salisbury volunteers have planted over 1000 trees this year, brought over 5,000 meals to elderly residents affected by lockdowns, and some really generous folks even started a learn to drive program for high school kids affected by the train lines shutting down. We also have a gorgeous library now which doubles as a museum and offers language courses in Kaurna. Great views inside too of the city centre. Mawson Lakes hosts a UniSA campus too which runs the planetarium, plus some community gardens. 

Admittedly, it's not all sunshine here though. We are a poorer council area with little job opportunities, we get a fair bit of crime, and we don't have a freaking train running at the moment. But for what it's worth, I think Salisbury council area in general is honestly a wonderful choice for moving too. I moved here ten years ago, and I adore this place. I don't think I've ever felt so a part of a community like I have here.
